exposure: suspected large for gestational age (LGA) fetus
control group (C) of women undergoing induction of labour on or after 280 days gestation
outcome: scan accuracy (PPV of EFW for birthweight)
cohort: The study included 845 induced pregnancies divided into three groups: women with a suspected LGA fetus, women with diabetes, and a control group of women induced on or after 280 days gestation.
finding: Third trimester estimated fetal weight (EFW) for bigger babies was poorly predictive of macrosomia, and although fetal outcomes were good, women selected and induced due to suspected LGA had higher rates of hemorrhage and intervention.
mod_finding: Women with suspected LGA had a significantly higher rate of assisted vaginal delivery (21.9% vs 16.5% in controls) and a significantly lower likelihood of spontaneous vaginal delivery (53.9% vs 68.7% in controls).
followup_time: Neonatal outcomes were assessed at birth or immediately postpartum, with no long-term follow-up mentioned.
birth_weight: Mean birthweights differed significantly between groups, and the study investigated birthweight >90th centile or >4 kg.
gest_age: Induction of labour occurred on or after 280 days gestation for the control group, and the study focused on large for gestational age (LGA) fetuses.
